eligibility: Bachelor's Degree programme: 12 years of education in the required subjects with at least 60% marks
Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy: F.Sc. or equivalent (Pre-Medical) with at least 65% marks
Engineering: F.Sc. or equivalent (Pre-Engineering) with at least 65% marks
Master's Degree programme: 16 years of education in relevant subjects with at least 3.00 CGP or 65% marks
Doctoral Degree programme: 18 years of education in relevant subjects with at least 3.00 CGP or 65% marks
Age limit of 17 to 23 years for BS programmes; maximum age of 35 years for doctoral programmes
requirements: Apply through the HEC scholarship portal
Candidates holding a foreign qualification must provide an Equivalence Certificate from IBCC and HEC
Accept the obligation to serve Bangladesh after completing education in Pakistan
Hold the requisite qualification on or before the last date of application submission
documents: Evidence of the qualifying examination result at the stated mark threshold
IBCC and HEC Equivalence Certificate where the qualification is foreign
selection_criteria: Academic thresholds set by level: 60% for Bachelor's, 65% for Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy and Engineering, 3.00 CGP or 65% for Master's and Doctoral programmes
Completion of the requisite qualification on or before the last date of application submission
application_method: Apply through the Higher Education Commission's scholarship portal
For queries, contact the Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor desk at HEC, Sector H-9, Islamabad
official.application_route: Online through HEC's scholarship portal under the Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor.
official.international_eligibility: Restricted to Bangladeshi citizens; the study itself takes place at Pakistani universities
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Medicine, engineering, computer science, business administration, mass communication, media studies, and basic and social sciences at Pakistani public and private universities
official.description: The Allama Muhammad Iqbal Scholarships for Students from Bangladesh are the student component of the Government of Pakistan's Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor, a bilateral initiative to strengthen ties between the two countries, under which HEC awards places to Bangladeshi citizens to study at Pakistani universities across Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a government-to-government route into Pakistani public and private universities for Bangladeshi nationals at Bachelor's, Master's and PhD level, and it is only worth preparing for if you accept a post-study service obligation to Bangladesh, because that obligation is a condition of the award. HEC publishes no stipend figure, so you should plan on the assumption that the monthly allowance may not cover your full living costs in Pakistan and keep a personal buffer. Because no closing date is published on the HEC pages, the window can open and shut at short notice, so check the Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor pages on the HEC site rather than relying on third-party listings. If any part of your education was completed outside Bangladesh, start your IBCC and HEC equivalence applications now, since they routinely take longer than the application window itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bangladeshi students with strong HSC, Bachelor's or Master's results who want a state-supported place at a Pakistani university and are willing to return home to serve afterwards.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your aggregate or CGP against the threshold for your level (60% for BS, 65% for Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy and Engineering, 3.00 CGP or 65% for Master's and PhD) and confirm your age is inside the 17-23 window for BS or under 35 for doctoral study
Start IBCC and HEC equivalence applications early if any qualification was obtained outside Bangladesh
Assemble mark sheets, transcripts and proof of Bangladeshi citizenship as clear scanned copies before the portal opens
Watch the HEC Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor pages weekly for the opening of the application window
Decide in advance whether you can accept the requirement to serve Bangladesh after graduation, and get the undertaking in writing if required
common_rejection_risks: Falling just below a level-specific threshold, particularly the 65% bar for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and engineering
Missing the IBCC or HEC equivalence certificate for a qualification obtained outside Bangladesh
Being outside the age window (17-23 for BS, 35 maximum for doctoral programmes)
Completing the qualifying examination after the closing date, which the published rules exclude
Submitting an incomplete portal application, since HEC routes everything through the scholarship portal with no paper fallback
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: HEC does not publish a stipend value, so the adequacy of the stipend against living costs in Pakistan cannot be checked. On the recorded package of tuition, stipend, hostel and mess charges, settlement allowance, air ticket and books, applicants should still expect to fund personal spending, visa and documentation fees, and any travel beyond the single provided ticket themselves.
document_audit: Equivalence certificates from IBCC and HEC are the classic bottleneck for applicants whose schooling is not Bangladeshi; they take weeks and cannot be produced overnight
Mark sheets and transcripts must show the exact aggregate or CGP claimed, so resolve any discrepancy with your board or university before applying
Proof of Bangladeshi citizenship must be current and match the name used on every academic document
alerts: No closing date is published on the pages read, so the application window can open and close without long notice
The obligation to serve Bangladesh after completing studies in Pakistan is a condition of the award, not a formality

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register and apply through HEC's scholarship portal for the Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor, upload results and any equivalence certificates, and direct queries to the PBKC desk at HEC in Islamabad while the application is assessed.
